comparisons.peer_summary: AMD focuses its R&D on designing next-generation CPUs, GPUs, FPGAs, Adaptive SoCs, accelerators, SOMs, and SmartNICs, along with associated software and hardware design tools.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies describe specific R&D focuses and product development milestones within their semiconductor businesses. Micron (MU) highlights specific technology nodes reaching production volume, such as 1-gamma DRAM with EUV lithography and Micron G9 NAND, indicating progress in manufacturing capabilities. Similarly, AMD outlines its R&D focus on designing next-generation processors (CPU/GPU) and accelerators using advanced semiconductor manufacturing processes, aiming for improved performance and power efficiency. While Micron details specific node introductions (1-gamma, G9) as production milestones, AMD describes its broader strategic focus on developing these next-generation integrated circuits and associated software tools.

sentences.text: Our 1-gamma DRAM pilot production using EUV lithography is progressing well, and we are on track for volume production in calendar 2025.
We have begun volume production on our Micron G9 NAND node, and expect to introduce several industry-leading products over the coming quarters.

Our main area of focus is on delivering the next generation of processors (CPU and GPU), FPGAs and Adaptive SoCs, accelerators (adaptive, graphics and DPU), SOMs and SmartNICs and associated software.

We focus on designing, with security in mind, new integrated circuits (ICs) with improved performance and performance-per-watt in advanced semiconductor manufacturing processes, the design of logic and interface IP, advanced packaging technologies, and heterogeneous integration technologies.

comparisons.peer_topic: 2024 Process Node Manufacturing Status and Roadmap Changes
comparisons.peer_summary: As of the end of 2024, most products were manufactured using the Intel 7 node, while high-volume production of the Intel 4 and Intel 3 nodes was shifted to Ireland. The company canceled the productization of Intel 20A to focus on the improved Intel 18A node, which is expected to enter high-volume production in 2025.
comparisons.comparison: Micron and Intel both discuss specific progress and roadmaps for advanced semiconductor process nodes and manufacturing volumes. Micron reports being on track for volume production of its 1-gamma DRAM node using EUV lithography in 2025 and beginning volume production of its G9 NAND node. Intel describes a similar landscape of advanced node transitions, noting that Intel 4 and Intel 3 were its first EUV lithography nodes which were ramped in 2024, and that it is focusing efforts on the Intel 18A node for high-volume production in 2025. Both disclosures highlight the industry-wide shift to EUV lithography and the specific timing of volume production for new technology nodes as key operational metrics.

sentences.text: Our 1-gamma DRAM pilot production using EUV lithography is progressing well, and we are on track for volume production in calendar 2025.

As of the end of 2024, a significant majority of our products were manufactured using our Intel 7 process node in Arizona and Israel, we successfully ramped our Intel 4 and Intel 3 process nodes as our first EUV lithography nodes and shifted high-volume production of those nodes to Ireland, and we canceled the productization of our Intel 20A process node to focus efforts on the improved version of the node, Intel 18A, that we expect to put into high-volume production in 2025 with our new client family of products code-named Panther Lake.

comparisons.peer_topic: Fabless manufacturing strategy and supplier responsibilities
comparisons.peer_summary: The company utilizes a fabless strategy, partnering with suppliers for wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, and packaging, while suppliers handle the procurement of most raw materials.
comparisons.comparison: The comparison centers on the structural approach to semiconductor product development and manufacturing. Micron discloses that it is on track for volume production of its 1-gamma DRAM and G9 NAND nodes, implying significant internal manufacturing and production capabilities for these memory products. In contrast, Nvidia explicitly states it utilizes a 'fabless and contracting manufacturing strategy,' partnering with key suppliers for all phases including wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, and packaging. This highlights a fundamental difference in operational model: Micron manages its own volume production facilities for its nodes, whereas Nvidia outsources these manufacturing phases to avoid the costs and risks of owning operations, allowing Nvidia to focus resources on design and marketing.

sentences.text: Our 1-gamma DRAM pilot production using EUV lithography is progressing well, and we are on track for volume production in calendar 2025.
We have begun volume production on our Micron G9 NAND node, and expect to introduce several industry-leading products over the coming quarters.

We utilize a fabless and contracting manufacturing strategy, whereby we employ and partner with key suppliers for all phases of the manufacturing process, including wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, and packaging.
Additionally, we can avoid many of the significant costs and risks associated with owning and operating manufacturing operations.
As a result, we can focus our resources on product design, quality assurance, marketing, and customer support.

comparisons.peer_topic: R&D investment scope and diversification targets
comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm expects to continue investing in research and development to extend product demand and utilize R&D in industries beyond mobile handsets, such as automotive, IoT, ADAS/AD, and XR, while also focusing on enabling developers to deploy applications across multiple device categories.
comparisons.comparison: Micron and Qualcomm both emphasize the role of continuous research and development in introducing new products and extending market demand. Micron states it expects to introduce 'industry-leading products' following the volume production of its G9 NAND node. Qualcomm states it expects to continue investing in R&D to 'extend the demand for our products and technologies' and utilize R&D in industries beyond mobile handsets. Both disclosures link their R&D investment directly to the introduction of new generations of technology and the expansion of their addressable markets, although Micron's example is specific to memory nodes while Qualcomm's is broader across multiple technology sectors.
